theme: 3 terms on initializers: how a type sets up a new value

terms.definition: A special method that sets up a new value of a type before you use it.
terms.example: Write an initializer, so every new user starts with a name.

terms.definition: An initializer that Swift gives a struct for free, with one parameter for each property.
terms.example: Use the memberwise initializer, so you do not write `init` by hand.

terms.definition: An initializer that can return `nil` when it cannot create a valid value.
terms.example: Make it a failable initializer, so a bad number returns `nil`.

video.title: Initializer, Memberwise & Failable Initializer | iOS Daily English Day 13
video.description:
Learn to talk about Swift initializers: Initializer, Memberwise Initializer and Failable Initializer, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Initializer - A special method that sets up a new value of a type before you use it.
Memberwise Initializer - An initializer that Swift gives a struct for free, with one parameter for each property.
Failable Initializer - An initializer that can return `nil` when it cannot create a valid value.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Day 13 of the iOS Daily English series: 3 terms a day, from Swift basics to advanced iOS.

landscape.description:
Explain Initializer, Memberwise Initializer and Failable Initializer in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
이니셜라이저, 멤버와이즈 이니셜라이저, 실패 가능한 이니셜라이저 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Initializer - A special method that sets up a new value of a type before you use it.
한국어: 타입의 새 값을 사용하기 전에 설정하는 특별한 메서드

Memberwise Initializer - An initializer that Swift gives a struct for free, with one parameter for each property.
한국어: Swift가 구조체에 자동으로 만들어 주는, 프로퍼티별 파라미터를 가진 이니셜라이저

Failable Initializer - An initializer that can return `nil` when it cannot create a valid value.
한국어: 유효한 값을 만들 수 없을 때 nil을 반환할 수 있는 이니셜라이저

dialogue.title: The Age check

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I added an initializer to `Age`, so it checks the number.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. An initializer sets up a new value before you use it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: But now `Age(value: 5)` fails. I used the memberwise initializer before.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Right. Swift gives a struct a memberwise initializer for free, but your own `init` removes it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: OK. What if the number is below zero?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Make it a failable initializer. Write `init?` and return `nil`.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So a failable initializer can give me `nil` instead of an `Age`?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. Check for `nil` before you use it.
